correctness.rationale: The exact source inequalities were reconstructed with all normal norms: 1 for coordinate walls, sqrt(i) for top/bottom prefix walls, and sqrt(2i) for inter-column prefix walls. At i=1 these radius inequalities telescope to \(1\ge r(2+(m-1)\sqrt2)\), giving the global upper bound. The explicit profile \(y_j=r(1+(m-j)\sqrt2)\) repeated in every row satisfies every higher-prefix inequality because \(i\ge\sqrt i\), proving sharpness. At equality all first-row inequalities used in the telescope are forced to equality, fixing the first row. A strict-slack witness in all remaining rows proves that no further affine equality is universal, so the incenter-set dimension is exactly m(n-1).

value.rationale: The generalized Pitman–Stanley polytope is a genuinely new m-column extension with active recent work on flow realizations, vertices, faces, volumes, and lattice points. The theorem gives a canonical metric invariant of a natural distinguished subfamily and reveals a non-obvious dimension-free phenomenon: increasing the row parameter changes the ambient dimension but not the inradius. It also completely separates radius rigidity from center nonuniqueness by proving that only the first row is forced while each additional row contributes m degrees of freedom. This is a family-wide structural metric statement rather than a finite computation or a routine single-parameter increment.
